study.subtitle: Turn a lecture into structured knowledge powered by CORTEXAI Neural Core.
study.summaryConnected: Connected to CORTEXAI Neural Processing Engine.
study.lecturePlaceholder: Paste your lecture notes, textbook excerpt, or any technical content here...
study.localQ1: What is the main principle described in this lecture?
study.localQ1Exp: The lecture discusses the CAP theorem which describes the fundamental trade-off between consistency, availability, and partition tolerance in distributed systems.
study.localQ2: Which replication strategy uses a designated leader node?
study.localQ2Exp: Leader-based replication uses a single leader node to coordinate writes, ensuring consistency across replicas.
study.localQ3: What happens during a network partition according to CAP?
study.localQ3A: The system chooses a trade-off between consistency and availability
study.localQ3Exp: During a network partition, a distributed system must choose between consistency (CP) or availability (AP) - it cannot guarantee both simultaneously.
study.localQ4: What should guide consistency choices in practice?
study.localQ4Exp: The lecture emphasizes that practical systems choose their position in the CAP design space based on user expectations and failure modes, not arbitrary preferences.
study.localQ5: What kind of consistency can replication produce?
study.localQ5Exp: Replication strategies can produce eventual consistency where replicas converge when updates stop, which is a practical compromise for many systems.
study.localCard1B: In a distributed system, you can only guarantee 2 of 3: Consistency, Availability, Partition Tolerance. During a partition, choose CP or AP.
study.localCard2B: One leader accepts writes, replicates to followers. Reads can go to leader (strong) or followers (eventual). Simple but leader is bottleneck.
study.localCard3B: Read from majority of replicas (W + R > N). Ensures you see latest write. Trades latency for consistency.
study.localCard4B: Replicas converge when updates stop. No strong guarantees but high availability. Used in DNS, DynamoDB, Cassandra.
study.localCard5B: Network partitions are inevitable in distributed systems. You MUST choose how to handle them: sacrifice C or A.
